clinician.trajectory_summary: A 47-year-old woman presented with a 10x12 cm fungating cauliflower-like mass on her right arm, which had grown rapidly over 3 months and was associated with intermittent fever, chills, weight loss, and bleeding. An X-ray of the right humerus showed a large hyperdense soft tissue mass. The patient underwent surgical resection of the mass (10 cm × 9 cm), and histopathology confirmed a malignant melanoma with necrosis (nodular melanoma type). A subsequent CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis was negative for metastasis.
